rejected.caption: Defines a classify_review function that encodes input text, checks the model context length, truncates and pads token IDs, and prepares them for model inference.
rejected.code:
def classify_review(text, model, tokenizer, device, max_length=None, pad_token_id=50256):
    model.eval()

    # Prepare inputs to the model
    input_ids = tokenizer.encode(text)
    supported_context_length = model.pos_emb.weight.shape[0]
    # Note: In the book, this was originally written as pos_emb.weight.shape[1] by mistake
    # It didn't break the code but would have caused unnecessary truncation (to 768 instead of 1024)

    # Truncate sequences if they too long
    input_ids = input_ids[:min(max_length, supported_context_length)]
    assert max_length is not None, (
        "max_length must be specified. If you want to use the full model context, "
        "pass max_length=model.pos_emb.weight.shape[0]."
    )
    assert max_length <= supported_context_length, (
        f"max_length ({max_length}) exceeds model's supported context length ({supported_context_length})."
    )    
    # Alternatively, a more robust version is the following one, which handles the max_length=None case better
    # max_len = min(max_length,supported_context_length) if max_length else supported_context_length
    # input_ids = input_ids[:max_len]
    
    # Pad sequences to the longest sequence
    input_ids += [pad_token_id] * (max_length - len(input_ids))
    input_tensor = torch.tensor(input_ids, device=device).unsqueeze(0) # add batch dimension

    # Model inference
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits = model(input_tensor)[:, -1, :]  # Logits of the last output token
    predicted_label = torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1).item()
rejected.reason: The code does define classify_review, encodes text to token IDs, checks supported context length from pos_emb, truncates and pads with token 50256, converts to a tensor, adds a batch dimension, runs inference, takes last-token logits, and argmaxes a label—matching much of the section and caption. However, it does not implement the section’s logic of comparing the training-set maximum token length with the model context length and using the smaller as the working max; instead it requires an explicit max_length and asserts it is <= supported_context_length. Also, it truncates using min(max_length, supported_context_length) before asserting max_length is not None, and it doesn’t map the predicted label to “spam/not spam” or show the test messages or saving/loading with torch.save/torch.load.
